items.title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors
items.summary:
arXiv:2611.17338v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM memory systems often delete facts classified as stale. We show that this hard-filtering step can reduce downstream accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts. Across three models, a controlled sensitivity intervention moves hard-drop from gains of +0.186 to +0.230 at perfect resolution to losses of -0.176 to -0.181 at the lowest tested reliability. items.reasoning: This paper finds that hard-deleting facts judged stale can hurt agent accuracy when the staleness resolver makes mistakes. That bears on how Meevo designs its memory and context for persistent business assistants, for example by preferring soft filtering over hard deletion. It does not change Claude API pricing or capabilities, and customers will not ask for it directly, though they do expect reliable recall.
